classification.difficultyReason: Read successive outputs from two graphs, evaluating the inner function before the outer function.

content.prompt: Using the graphs below, evaluate $f(g(1))$ and $g(f(2))$.

spec.description: Upward parabola on a unit grid, with vertex (3,-1), roots 2 and 4, and continuation arrows at its upper ends. Paired with the f graph on its right.
spec.mathematics: g(x)=(x-3)^2-1; displayed grid x=-2 to 7 and y=-5 to 7.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph remains visible in the student edition; no evaluation annotations are included.

spec.description: Downward parabola on a unit grid, with vertex (3,6), passing through (0,-3), (1,2), (2,5), (4,5), (5,2) and (6,-3), with continuation arrows at its lower ends.
spec.mathematics: f(x)=6-(x-3)^2; displayed grid x=-2 to 7 and y=-5 to 7.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph remains visible in the student edition; no evaluation annotations are included.

answer.worked:
From the graphs, $g(1)=3$ and $f(3)=6$.
$$\begin{align*}f(g(1))&=f(3)\\f(g(1))&=6\end{align*}$$
Also, $f(2)=5$ and $g(5)=3$.
$$\begin{align*}g(f(2))&=g(5)\\g(f(2))&=3\end{align*}$$
